analysis.investment_thesis: Equitas SFB is a mid-cap bank (₹7,490 Cr) far outside my SMILE sweet spot, trading at 51x trailing P/E with ROE collapsed to 2.42% — profits fell 82% YoY (₹799 Cr → ₹147 Cr). The structural problem is clear: finance costs are compounding at 29.1% CAGR while revenue grows at only 17.4%, destroying the spread.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR of 17.4% over 3 years shows top-line momentum in underpenetrated microfinance and SFB space
Balance sheet nearly doubled (₹26,948 Cr → ₹52,836 Cr in 3 years), indicating strong deposit franchise growth
Forward P/E of 11.28x implies market expects a sharp profit recovery — if it materialises, there's re-rating potential
key_risks: Finance costs exploding at 29.1% CAGR vs. revenue at 17.4% — NIM compression is structural, not cyclical
Net profit crashed 82% in FY2025 (₹799 Cr → ₹147 Cr); ROE of 2.42% is unacceptable for any bank
Market cap of ₹7,490 Cr is 4-7x outside my small-cap sweet spot — no information asymmetry, heavily DII-owned (50.87%)
red_flags: Trailing P/E of 50.93x for a bank earning near-zero returns is a valuation trap
No promoter holding disclosed — RBI-mandated dilution for SFBs removes the 'skin in the game' criterion entirely
Finance cost CAGR (29.1%) outpacing revenue CAGR (17.4%) by 1,170 bps annually — structural spread erosion
Net profit CAGR of -19.4% over 3 years despite balance sheet doubling — scale is not generating returns
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Equitas SFB fails the SMILE test on almost every dimension. At ₹7,490 Cr market cap, it is a mid-cap institution well past the discovery phase — DII ownership at 50.87% confirms this is a crowded, well-followed name with no information edge. The trailing P/E of 50.93x for a bank delivering 2.42% ROE is a classic value trap: the market is pricing in a massive profit recovery (implied by 11.28x forward P/E), but the structural headwind of rising cost of funds (finance costs up 29% CAGR) makes that recovery uncertain. Profits collapsed 82% in FY2025 even as the balance sheet and revenues kept growing — a clear sign that asset quality stress and/or funding cost pressures are eating the entire spread.

From a Kedia SMILE lens, the core problem is there is no transformation inflection visible here — only deterioration. A true multibagger in the SFB space would show ROE accelerating past 15%, promoter conviction with >50% holding, and margins expanding as scale kicks in. Equitas shows the opposite: margin contraction, profit implosion, and institutional saturation. The only scenario for investment would be a confirmed NIM recovery, improved asset quality, and re-rating on forward earnings — but that is a turnaround trade, not a SMILE multibagger. I would rather wait for cleaner signals or find a smaller, undiscovered NBFC/MFI at an earlier stage of the journey.
